content: Pseudodiarrhea, previously referred to as hyperdefecation, is characterized by an increased frequency of bowel movements, defined as more than three times per day, while maintaining a normal daily stool weight of less than 300 grams (Fine and Schiller, 1999). This condition is frequently associated with rectal urgency and is commonly observed in conjunction with irritable bowel syndrome, hyperthyroidism, and anorectal disorders such as proctitis. Additionally, pseudodiarrhea can occur in cases of fecal impaction or obstruction caused by factors such as a vaginal pessary. In these situations, only liquid stool is able to pass through the obstruction, leading to the presentation of pseudodiarrhea (Chou and Yu, 2003; Tatar and Trivedi, 2005). It is important to note that pseudodiarrhea may be more prevalent than chronic diarrhea and should always be considered as a differential diagnosis in patients presenting with complaints of chronic diarrhea.
